jobs.title: Full Stack Technology Lead - Vice President
jobs.description:
Citi is looking for a Full Stack Technology Lead to join its Technology team and shape the next generation of scalable, AI-augmented engineering. In this Vice President-level role, you will own end-to-end technical delivery — from architecting robust full-stack systems to pioneering the use of agentic AI workflows that transform how software is built at scale. This is an opportunity to lead at the intersection of modern engineering and cutting-edge AI tooling, directly influencing how Citi's engineering teams operate and deliver.

Responsibilities

Design, develop, and maintain scalable full-stack applications using ReactJS, TypeScript, and Python, translating complex business requirements into well-structured technical architecture and design documentation.
Contribute to system architecture decisions — spanning monolith versus microservices trade-offs, database design, and API strategy — to ensure solutions are robust, maintainable, and built for scale.
Lead the adoption of AI-assisted development tooling as a primary engineering accelerator, covering feature scaffolding, automated test authoring, code refactoring, and documentation generation.
Design and implement agentic engineering workflows that autonomously handle multi-step tasks including issue triage, code review assistance, pull request generation, and deployment scripting.
Identify and prototype opportunities where agentic AI can reduce manual effort across the software delivery lifecycle, including automated bug fixes, test generation, and dependency management.
Establish prompt engineering standards and quality gates for AI-generated code, ensuring outputs consistently meet security, correctness, and maintainability requirements.
Support CI/CD pipeline development and release strategies, ensuring smooth, reliable delivery of production-grade software.

Required Qualifications & Skills

6 or more years of full-stack development using ReactJS and TypeScript, with deep proficiency in hooks, context, and state management libraries such as Redux, Zustand, or Recoil.
Advanced TypeScript capability including generics, decorators, and complex typing strategies, paired with strong Python development skills in modular, middleware-driven architectures.
Expert-level knowledge of API design — REST and GraphQL — covering versioning, error handling, and performance optimisation at production scale.
Proven ability to design distributed systems, with proficiency across SQL and NoSQL databases, event-driven architecture, and messaging technologies such as Kafka or RabbitMQ.
Hands-on experience integrating and directing AI agent-led coding workflows within a production engineering environment.
Solid command of modern HTML and CSS, including responsive design principles, accessibility standards, and component library or design system implementation.
Working knowledge of DevOps practices and tooling including Docker, Kubernetes, Terraform, and CI/CD pipeline configuration.

Beneficial Skills & Qualifications

Bachelor's degree or equivalent practical experience in a relevant technical discipline.
Master's degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, or a related field.
Experience evaluating and integrating emerging AI coding capabilities into team toolchains, with a track record of staying current with agentic AI developments.

What We Offer

At Citi, you will work on engineering challenges that operate at genuine global scale, collaborating with high-performing teams across technology and business. This role offers the scope, autonomy, and resources to make a lasting impact on how modern financial technology is built and delivered.

Hybrid working model with 3 days in the office and 2 days working remotely, giving you flexibility and consistent team connection.
A technically ambitious environment where you can lead real engineering innovation, including pioneering agentic AI adoption across the software delivery lifecycle.
Access to continuous learning and development resources to keep your technical skills at the leading edge of the industry.
Competitive compensation and financial wellbeing benefits reflecting the seniority and strategic impact of the role.
Wellbeing and work-life balance support, including programmes designed to sustain performance and personal resilience over the long term.
Global collaboration across a technology organisation of significant scale, with exposure to cross-functional teams and complex, high-impact systems.

Build the future of AI-augmented engineering at Citi — apply now and bring your technical leadership to one of the world's most consequential technology organisations.

jobs.description:
Position Title:
Director, Supply Chain Network Strategy & Design

Position Type:
Regular - Full-Time

Grade:
Grade 07

Requisition ID:
43306

In every role, McCainers are ambitious, curious, and passionate about creating exceptional work experiences - together. With a customer-first mindset, we make doing business with McCain easy.

About The Role.

The Director, Supply Chain Network Strategy & Design owns how and where McCain makes, sources, and stores finished goods for the Global Snacking business — translating commercial ambition into a resilient, cost-advantaged manufacturing and distribution footprint.

Reporting to the VP, Supply Chain – Global Snacking, and building a new, purpose-built team, this leader sets the finished-goods sourcing and network strategy: the make-vs-buy decisions, footprint choices, and product-to-plant-to-market flows that determine how Snacking will scale Globally. This is a strategy-and-design mandate focused on the finished-goods network.

Success depends on strong cross-regional relationships and the ability to align diverse stakeholders behind common network outcomes — working closely with Regional Managing Directors across all regions (NA, EMENA, APACSA, LATAM) so local execution supports a single, high-performing global network. This newly created role offers the opportunity to build a new team and shape the function from the ground up.

What You’ll Be Doing.

Finished-Goods Network Strategy

Own the Global Snacking finished-goods network strategy — defining where products are manufactured, co-manufactured, and stored to serve each market at the best total delivered cost, service, and risk position.
Lead make-vs-buy strategy end to end: when to scale internally, when to keep or expand external/co-manufacturing, and how the footprint should evolve to support growth, new categories, and capacity needs.
Provide network and footprint inputs into long-range capacity and capital planning, in partnership with Operations, Finance, and Global Supply Chain.

Portfolio Segmentation

Define and maintain the strategic direction for every finished-goods product — Develop, Scale, Insource, Outsource, or Exit — with a simple, repeatable process to keep that view current as the business evolves.

Make-vs-Buy Governance & Decision Rights

Translate portfolio choices into a repeatable governance system: clear decision rights, owners, triggers, and review cadence for how make-vs-buy and network decisions are made and re-visited.
Establish the standards, criteria, and forums that let McCain make these calls consistently and defensibly across regions — rather than case by case.

Network Modeling, Scenario Planning & Analytics

Stand up and lead the network-modeling capability — using optimization and scenario tools to pressure-test footprint, sourcing, capacity, and flow decisions.
Run “what-if” scenarios (demand shifts, capacity constraints, cost/tariff changes, supply disruptions) to recommend optimal sourcing and deployment strategies with clear cost-to-serve transparency.

Regulatory & Trade Integration

Demonstrate a practical understanding of food and trade regulatory frameworks sufficient to engage effectively with Scientific & Regulatory Affairs (SRA) and trade-compliance teams, translating their requirements into operational network and sourcing decisions.
Embed regulatory and trade requirements into end-to-end network design — so compliance is proactively built into how product is designed, sourced, made, and moved globally.

Cross-Regional Partnership & Stakeholder Alignment

Act as a trusted advisor to Regional Managing Directors and Supply Chain Leads, aligning regional execution with the global network strategy.
Partner across Operations, Finance, Procurement, and Global Supply Chain to reconcile network recommendations with performance, cost, and investment realities — and to drive decisions to closure.

Team Leadership & Capability Building

Build, coach, and develop a new high-performing team (Manager, Network Strategy + two Supply Chain Analysts), establishing the ways of working, tools, and standards of this net-new function.
Foster a “One Supply Chain” mindset — connectivity, shared accountability, and continuous improvement across all Snacking regions.

What You’ll Need To Be Successful.

University degree in Supply Chain, Engineering, Operations Research, Analytics, or Business (Master’s preferred)
10+ years of progressive supply chain experience in multinational or FMCG/CPG environments
Deep expertise in network design, make-vs-buy strategy, footprint optimization, and capacity planning
Strong hands-on experience with network optimization tools (e.g., Llamasoft, Coupa Supply Chain Guru, Cosmic Frog or equivalent)
Advanced analytics capability, including total delivered cost and cost-to-serve modeling
Working knowledge of food and trade regulatory requirements and global trade compliance considerations
Proven ability to lead complex, cross-functional initiatives and influence senior stakeholders in global matrix organizations
Strong communication, facilitation, and relationship-building skills
Proficiency in SAP (or equivalent ERP), advanced Excel, and executive-level PowerPoint
Demonstrated success building and developing high-performing teams
Alignment with McCain’s values of authenticity, integrity, and people-first leadership

Additional Information.

Travel: Up to 20%, including international travel.
Work model: Hybrid — 3 days on-site (subject to change; most office-based roles follow McCain’s hybrid model with up to two days remote per week).

About The Team.

This is a newly established, high-impact team within Global Snacking Supply Chain. The Director will build and lead a team consisting of a Manager, Network Strategy and two Supply Chain Analysts. The team is responsible for establishing the frameworks, tools, and capabilities that enable a globally integrated network strategy, working closely with regional teams and cross-functional partners across Operations, Finance, Procurement, and Supply Chain.

About McCain.

At McCain, you’ll be part of a collaborative, people-first culture that values curiosity, continuous improvement, and shared success. We foster an inclusive environment where employees are empowered to grow, contribute ideas, and make a meaningful impact.

This role follows a hybrid work model, with team members typically working onsite three days per week and remotely up to two days, offering flexibility while maintaining strong team connection.

Description

Senior Director, Enterprise Architecture

CTO Office - Information Technology Vice-Presidency (ITVP)

Build the Future with Us

Position Context

At a time when artificial intelligence, automation, and digital platforms are redefining the pace of change in financial services, the Information Technology Vice-Presidency is seeking to strengthen its ability to drive a comprehensive, cohesive, and forward-looking enterprise architecture vision.

Reporting to the CTO within the CTO Office, the Senior Director, Enterprise Architecture plays a critical role in evolving enterprise architecture from a function primarily focused on alignment and governance into a strategic capability that accelerates transformation, simplification, and enterprise-wide AI adoption.

Your Mission

As the leader responsible for transforming the Architecture function, the Senior Director, Enterprise Architecture is accountable for defining, championing, and evolving the enterprise architecture vision across information, application, and technology domains while supporting business sectors in their transformation initiatives. The incumbent shapes the foundations that will enable iA to evolve into an AI-augmented enterprise, where data, platforms, processes, and digital capabilities can scale rapidly, securely, and efficiently.

Working in close partnership with senior architects and domain experts, the Senior Director creates the conditions that enable architectural expertise to have greater impact, faster, on organizational decisions and transformations.

Complementing the role of the Senior Director, Business Architecture and Innovation, this position is responsible for enterprise technology directions, principles, and architectures, while the other role is responsible for business capability and value stream architecture.

What You Will Accomplish With Us

Enterprise Architecture Vision and Strategic Direction

Define and maintain an integrated enterprise architecture vision aligned with the organization’s strategic priorities and its ambition to become a more AI-augmented enterprise.
Establish and evolve target technology architectures, principles, and directions, while exercising decision-making authority over them.
Ensure alignment between business models and priorities, organizational capabilities, key processes, and application and technology architectures, while identifying opportunities for simplification and acceleration.
Define target architectures and evolution roadmaps that modernize platforms, reduce complexity, and accelerate value delivery.

IT 2030 Plan, Roadmaps, and the ITE4B Portfolio

Lead the IT 2030 plan across all business lines and domains, coordinating its execution while managing dependencies and priorities.
Ensure business sector roadmaps remain aligned with enterprise-wide directions.
Oversee the ITE4B (IT Enablers for Business) portfolio under delegated authority from the CTO, ensuring architectural and technological consistency while aligning initiatives with target architectures, the simplification strategy, and the IT 2030 plan.
Lead prioritization and investment arbitration processes for the ITE4B portfolio by making dependencies and initiative value visible and reporting to the CTO and CIO in collaboration with the Corporate Project Office and business sectors, while preserving accountability for major decisions at the sector level.

Modernization of the Enterprise Architecture Practice

Reinvent the enterprise architecture practice to support the pace of transformation required in the age of artificial intelligence while maintaining robustness, security, and compliance within a regulated environment.
Leverage generative AI, automation, and modern engineering approaches to accelerate artifact production, impact analysis, documentation, and architectural decision-making.
Evolve the architecture function toward a practice focused more on influence, reuse, platforms, and business outcomes than on documentation production.

Business and IT Alignment and Convergence

Foster long-term alignment between business needs and architectural choices by positioning architecture as a strategic accelerator rather than a control function.
Translate business challenges into coherent architectural capabilities.
Position enterprise architecture as the integration point for AI, data, cybersecurity, and technology strategies, ensuring the foundations required for their responsible scaling.
Champion iAFG’s IT strategy and ensure its alignment with business, innovation, and AI roadmaps, in close collaboration with the Senior Director, Business Architecture and Innovation.

Governance and Architectural Leadership

Design and lead governance mechanisms that accelerate key decisions, clarify trade-offs, and reduce ambiguity.
Establish architecture directions, principles, standards, and positions on major and cross-functional initiatives, emphasizing clear, actionable, and risk-proportionate guidance.
Support executive decision-making bodies through clear and structured analysis while helping resolve complex cross-functional issues.
Define enterprise architecture standards and frameworks that support strong governance and enable increasing integration with platforms, processes, and delivery tools.
In collaboration with Risk Management, define AI and agent governance principles and architectural control layers, including auditability, autonomy boundaries, and data traceability.
Accelerate architecture decisions by equipping the practice with templates, reusable components, and pre-approved decisions for priority initiatives, ensuring that the compliant path is also the simplest one.

Leadership and Team Development

Provide strong leadership to enterprise architecture directors and teams through clear direction, senior expertise, and empowerment.
Unite stakeholders around a shared vision by acting as an effective communicator and negotiator.
Build future-ready capabilities and support the growth and development of architecture talent.

What Will Help You Succeed In This Role

Education and Experience

University degree in Information Technology, Engineering, Business Administration, or a related field.
Significant experience in enterprise architecture, IT strategy, or organizational transformation, including leadership responsibilities and transformation of professional practices.
Strong understanding of business models and complex IT environments.
Experience collaborating with executive-level stakeholders.
Knowledge of trends in artificial intelligence, data, cybersecurity, automation, and emerging architectures, as well as their implications within a regulated financial services environment (an asset).

Key Competencies

Broad organizational and systems-thinking perspective.
Ability to guide technology decisions while leveraging the expertise of senior architects and domain specialists.
Strong analytical and synthesis skills with the ability to put complex and cross-functional issues into perspective.
Excellent communication and influence skills at strategic levels.
Strong negotiation skills and the ability to unite stakeholders around a common vision.
Ability to advance strategic initiatives over both short- and medium-term horizons, with a strong focus on execution speed, simplification, and value creation.
Advanced proficiency in both French and English, as the incumbent will be required to collaborate daily, both verbally and in writing, with unilingual English-speaking partners, teams, and stakeholders across Canada and internationally.

WHO WE ARE

GreenShield is a proudly Canadian, national non-profit health care and insurance organization, driven by our mission of Better Health for All. We believe health care is a right, not a privilege, and we are committed to improving health outcomes, advancing health equity, and building a future where every Canadian can reach their full health and well-being potential.

Through our unique integrated payer-provider ("payvider") model, we offer insurance, administer benefits, and pay claims as a ‘payer’ while offering health care services such as mental health, pharmacy, telemedicine, and chronic disease management as a ‘provider’. As a non-profit social enterprise without shareholders, we reinvest our excess earnings to directly support underserved communities. Through GreenShield Cares, we positively impacted the health and well-being of over one million Canadians between 2020 and 2025. What’s driving us now is the commitment to measurably impact an additional three million Canadians by 2030 – across mental health, essential medicines, and chronic disease management – through scalable initiatives that deliver meaningful change in pursuit of our mission of Better Health for All.

At GreenShield, our culture is where purpose meets passion and performance. Our teams work as one to deliver meaningful, measurable impact for the people and communities we serve.

THE ROLE IN A NUTSHELL

The Vice-President, Enterprise Onboarding & Operations Optimization is accountable for leading GreenShield’s enterprise onboarding, enrollment, and implementation functions, ensuring the seamless, accurate, and scalable implementation of clients, plans, and members across all GreenShield portfolios (Group and Individual Insurance, Claims Adjudication, Benefits Administration, Third-Party Administration (TPA), and Health services).

This role is responsible for delivering a consistent, high-quality onboarding, enrollment and implementation experience that enables operational readiness, supports growth, and protects the client and member experience from day one.

Through these capabilities, the role ensures strong internal stakeholder partnership, coordinated resolution of operational issues, and clear performance visibility from frontline operations through to executive leadership.

We’re looking for a strategic and execution-oriented leader with deep experience building and scaling complex operational functions, and a strong track record of improving quality, speed, transparency, and experience through process discipline, stakeholder partnership, and technology enablement.

This leader brings credibility with senior stakeholders, strong operational judgment, and the ability to balance hands-on execution with enterprise-level thinking. QUI NOUS SOMMES

Daily tous les jours est un studio d'art et de design de renommée internationale, qui dirige un nouveau champ de pratique alliant l'art interactif, la narration, la performance et le design urbain pour réinventer le vivre ensemble au 21e siècle. Avec l’espace public que l’on partage tous les jours comme terrain de jeu, le studio explore les dynamiques de coopération entre les individus, en proposant de nouveaux modèles de vivre ensemble.

L’OPPORTUNITÉ

Nous concevons la prochaine génération de nos œuvres interactives : des expériences brevetables, entièrement autonomes, sans fil et alimentées à l’énergie solaire. Nous nous appuyons sur nos 15 ans d’expérience pour imaginer à quoi ressembleront les 15 prochaines années.
Il s’agit d’un véritable défi de R&D : nœuds multimedia embarqués distribués (distributed embedded nodes), synchronisation sans fil, autonomie énergétique en extérieur et plateforme logicielle permettant de mettre à jour et surveiller les contenus à distance. Nous recherchons un·e directeur·trice des technologies (CTO) capable de porter la vision technique de cette plateforme et d’encadrer l’équipe qui la concrétisera. Une personne tout aussi à l’aise pour lire un schéma électronique, réviser une architecture de micrologiciel (firmware), spécifier une capacité solaire, collaborer avec des designers industriels et présenter une feuille de route produit.

VOTRE RÔLE

Définir et prendre en charge l’architecture technique de nouvelles plateformes : matériel embarqué (embedded hardware), micrologiciel, réseaux sans fil, gestion de l’énergie et plateforme logicielle à distance.
Monter et diriger une équipe d’ingénierie agile, en commençant par un·e développeur·se de micrologiciel embarqué et un·e directeur·trice de produit, puis en l’élargissant avec des ingénieur·e·s matériel et logiciel dédié·e·s.
Piloter le cycle complet de R&D, de la preuve de concept jusqu’à la conception pour la fabrication (DFM), en passant par les phases alpha et les pilotes sur le terrain.
Définir et protéger la propriété intellectuelle.
Agir à titre d'interlocuteur·trice technique principal·e auprès des partenaires externes, des conseiller·ère·s, des organismes subventionnaires (PARI-CNRC) et des partenaires de déploiement pilote.
Collaborer directement avec l’équipe créative pour veiller à ce que la technologie serve et rehausse l’expérience utilisateur.
Établir des pratiques d’ingénierie, des outils et des normes de documentation permettant à la plateforme de passer à une échelle de plusieurs milliers d’unités par an.
En utilisant cette plateforme comme point de départ, travailler avec l’équipe technique actuelle pour transformer nos œuvres uniques passées en une base partagée afin de développer de nouveaux produits et expériences.

VOTRE PROFIL

Plus de 10 ans d’expérience en systèmes embarqués, en développement de produits matériel-logiciel ou dans une discipline d’ingénierie connexe.
Expérience concrète dans la conduite d’un produit matériel du prototype à la production à grande échelle (conception de PCB, micrologiciels, boîtiers, bancs d’essai et chaîne d'approvisionnement).
Maîtrise approfondie des architectures embarquées sans fil : Wi-Fi, BLE, réseaux maillés (mesh), protocoles de synchronisation temporelle. Expérience avec les composants de type Espressif : un atout majeur.
Expérience pratique en gestion de l’énergie : systèmes de batteries, recharge solaire, conception faible consommation (low-power), gestion thermique en extérieur.
Capacité démontrée à diriger et faire grandir des équipes d’ingénierie dans un environnement émergent et aux ressources limitées. Vous savez quand concevoir sur mesure et quand acheter une solution existante.
Expérience de la conception pour des conditions extérieures rigoureuses, de la conformité réglementaire (CE, FCC, indices IP) et du rendement de fabrication.
Aisance à travailler au sein d’un studio créatif interdisciplinaire à taille humaine. Vous comprenez que les décisions techniques façonnent directement des expériences humaines dans l’espace public.
Bilinguisme fonctionnel (français et anglais).

ATOUTS

Expérience avec les systèmes audio : traitement numérique du signal (DSP), conception d’haut-parleurs, amplification audio en contexte embarqué.
Connaissance des plateformes infonuagiques pour la gestion de flottes IoT et les mises à jour à distance du micrologiciel (OTA).
Parcours en art interactif, en design d’expérience ou en installations publiques.
Expérience dans la rédaction de demandes de subventions ou la gestion de programmes de financement en R&D.

CE QUE NOUS OFFRONS

Un projet techniquement ambitieux doté d’une véritable portée créative. La technologie que vous développerez sera expérimentée par des milliers de personnes dans des villes du monde entier.
Un studio collaboratif à échelle humaine (environ 15 personnes) où les décisions se prennent rapidement et où votre travail a un impact direct.
Environnement de travail basé à Montréal.
Occasions de voyager pour des installations et des déploiements pilotes.
Accès à un réseau de conseiller·ère·s de calibre mondial en réseaux de capteurs sans fil et systèmes embarqués.

NOTRE ENGAGEMENT

Daily tous les jours s’engage à bâtir une équipe inclusive qui reflète la diversité des espaces publics pour lesquels nous concevons. Nous accueillons les candidatures de tous horizons, identités et parcours. Nous vous encourageons à postuler même si vous ne répondez pas à la totalité des critères.

--

Daily tous les jours is an award-winning art and design studio working in an emergent field of practice combining interactive art, storytelling, performance, and urban design to reinvent living together for the 21st century. Using the raw material of the everyday, their work explores the dynamics of cooperation between people in proposing new models of living together.

THE OPPORTUNITY

We are building the next generation of our interactive artworks: patent-pending, fully self-contained, wireless, solar-powered experiences that create collective music without a single cable or technician on site. Building on our existing 15 years of experience to imagine the next 15.
This is a genuine R&D challenge: distributed embedded nodes, wireless synchronization, outdoor power autonomy, and a software platform to update and monitor installations remotely. We need a CTO who can hold the technical vision for this platform and nurture the team that will make it real, a person who is equally at home reading a schematic, reviewing firmware architecture, specifying solar power capacity, collaborating with industrial designers and presenting a product roadmap.

WHAT YOU WILL DO

Define and own the technical architecture of this new platform: embedded hardware, firmware, wireless networking, power management, and the remote software platform.
Build and lead a small, focused engineering team starting with an embedded firmware developer and a product owner, growing into dedicated hardware and software engineers.
Drive the full R&D cycle from proof-of-concept through alpha, outdoor field pilot, and design-for-manufacturing.
Define and protect intellectual property.
Act as the primary technical interlocutor for external partners, advisors, grant bodies (NRC IRAP), and pilot deployment partners.
Collaborate directly with the creative team to ensure the technology serves and elevates the experience.
Establish engineering practices, tooling, and documentation standards that allow the platform to scale to thousands of units per year.
Using this platform as a starting point, work with the existing technical team to help turn our legacy of one-off artworks into a shared foundation to develop more products and experiences.

WHAT YOU BRING

10+ years of experience in embedded systems, hardware-software product development, or a related engineering discipline.
Demonstrated experience taking a hardware product from prototype to manufacturing at scale. You have dealt with PCB design, firmware, enclosures, test fixtures, and supply chain.
Deep fluency in wireless embedded architectures: Wi-Fi, BLE, mesh networking, time-synchronization protocols. Experience with Espressif-class devices is a strong asset.
Hands-on experience with power management: battery systems, solar charging, low-power design, outdoor thermal management.
Proven ability to lead and grow engineering teams in an early-stage, resource-constrained environment. You know when to build and when to buy.
Experience designing for harsh outdoor conditions, regulatory compliance (CE, FCC, IP ratings), and manufacturing yield.
Comfort working in a small, cross-disciplinary creative studio. You understand that the technical decisions here directly shape human experiences in public space.

NICE TO HAVE

Experience with audio systems: DSP, speaker design, audio amplification in embedded contexts.
Familiarity with cloud platforms for IoT fleet management and OTA firmware updates.
Background in interactive art, experience design, or public installations.
Experience writing grant applications or managing R&D funding programs.
Functional bilingualism (French and English).

WHAT WE OFFER

A technically ambitious project with real creative purpose. The technology you build will be experienced by thousands of people in cities around the world.
A collaborative, human-scale studio (around 15 people) where decisions happen fast and your work has direct impact.
Work environment based in Montréal.
Opportunities to travel for installations and pilot deployments.
Access to a network of world-class advisors in wireless sensor networks and embedded systems.

OUR COMMITMENT

Daily tous les jours is committed to building an inclusive team that reflects the diversity of the public spaces we design for. We welcome candidates of all backgrounds, identities, and experiences. We encourage you to apply even if you do not meet every single requirement.
We thank all applicants for their interest in this position; however, only those we wish to interview will be contacted.

The Director, Supply Chain Network Strategy & Design owns how and where McCain makes, sources, and stores finished goods for the Global Snacking business — translating commercial ambition into a resilient, cost-advantaged manufacturing and distribution footprint.

Reporting to the VP, Supply Chain – Global Snacking, and building a new, purpose-built team, this leader sets the finished-goods sourcing and network strategy: the make-vs-buy decisions, footprint choices, and product-to-plant-to-market flows that determine how Snacking will scale Globally. This is a strategy-and-design mandate focused on the finished-goods network.

Success depends on strong cross-regional relationships and the ability to align diverse stakeholders behind common network outcomes — working closely with Regional Managing Directors across all regions (NA, EMENA, APACSA, LATAM) so local execution supports a single, high-performing global network. This newly created role offers the opportunity to build a new team and shape the function from the ground up.

What You’ll Be Doing.

Finished-Goods Network Strategy

Own the Global Snacking finished-goods network strategy — defining where products are manufactured, co-manufactured, and stored to serve each market at the best total delivered cost, service, and risk position.
Lead make-vs-buy strategy end to end: when to scale internally, when to keep or expand external/co-manufacturing, and how the footprint should evolve to support growth, new categories, and capacity needs.
Provide network and footprint inputs into long-range capacity and capital planning, in partnership with Operations, Finance, and Global Supply Chain.

Portfolio Segmentation

Define and maintain the strategic direction for every finished-goods product — Develop, Scale, Insource, Outsource, or Exit — with a simple, repeatable process to keep that view current as the business evolves.

Make-vs-Buy Governance & Decision Rights

Translate portfolio choices into a repeatable governance system: clear decision rights, owners, triggers, and review cadence for how make-vs-buy and network decisions are made and re-visited.
Establish the standards, criteria, and forums that let McCain make these calls consistently and defensibly across regions — rather than case by case.

Network Modeling, Scenario Planning & Analytics

Stand up and lead the network-modeling capability — using optimization and scenario tools to pressure-test footprint, sourcing, capacity, and flow decisions.
Run “what-if” scenarios (demand shifts, capacity constraints, cost/tariff changes, supply disruptions) to recommend optimal sourcing and deployment strategies with clear cost-to-serve transparency.

Regulatory & Trade Integration

Demonstrate a practical understanding of food and trade regulatory frameworks sufficient to engage effectively with Scientific & Regulatory Affairs (SRA) and trade-compliance teams, translating their requirements into operational network and sourcing decisions.
Embed regulatory and trade requirements into end-to-end network design — so compliance is proactively built into how product is designed, sourced, made, and moved globally.

Cross-Regional Partnership & Stakeholder Alignment

Act as a trusted advisor to Regional Managing Directors and Supply Chain Leads, aligning regional execution with the global network strategy.
Partner across Operations, Finance, Procurement, and Global Supply Chain to reconcile network recommendations with performance, cost, and investment realities — and to drive decisions to closure.

Team Leadership & Capability Building

Build, coach, and develop a new high-performing team (Manager, Network Strategy + two Supply Chain Analysts), establishing the ways of working, tools, and standards of this net-new function.

About ERA

The Electronic Recycling Association (ERA) is a Canadian non-profit organization founded in 2004. We are ISO-certified (27001, 9001, 14001, 45001) and dedicated to reducing e-waste while bridging the digital divide. We collect, securely wipe or destroy data from, refurbish, and donate computers, laptops, servers, and other IT equipment to charities, schools, and community organizations across Canada. With depots and pickup services in major cities from Vancouver to Halifax, ERA combines environmental responsibility, data security excellence, and community impact.

The Opportunity

We are seeking an influential, industry-respected leader
to join our Board of Directors in a paid advisory capacity
. This is not a traditional volunteer board seat — it is a compensated strategic role for a seasoned executive who will actively help shape ERA’s future.
As a Board Member with CIO-level expertise, you will provide high-impact guidance on technology strategy, data security innovation, IT asset management best practices, and network expansion. You will leverage your industry relationships to strengthen and grow ERA’s national and international partnerships.

Key Responsibilities

Advise the leadership team and board on IT infrastructure, cybersecurity, data destruction standards, and emerging technologies in e-waste management.
Help expand and optimize our national network of depots, corporate partners, charities, and refurbishment partners.
Provide strategic input on operational scalability, digital transformation, and new revenue/diversification opportunities.
Open doors to new corporate, government, and non-profit relationships that advance our mission.
Participate in quarterly board meetings and be available for ad-hoc strategic consultations (estimated 4–8 hours per month).

What We’re Looking For

Proven CIO, CTO, or equivalent senior technology executive experience
in IT asset disposition, e-waste recycling, data center operations, cybersecurity, or related industries.
Strong existing network in technology, sustainability, circular economy, or non-profit sectors.
Demonstrated success scaling operations, building partnerships, and driving innovation.
Passion for environmental sustainability, digital inclusion, and responsible IT asset management.

The Director Financial Advisory Services is responsible for providing strategic direction and technical leadership in the development of fiscal management strategy to assist the province in meeting its shared services objectives.
